newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy anti-trust probes Telecom tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Italy anti-trust probes Telecom tariffs.

text.p: Italy's anti-trust authority said on Friday it was launching an investigation into tariff discounts offered to clients by Telecom Italia to determine whether the company has abused a dominant market position.
The authority said in a statement that Telecom had been offering discounts of up to 30 percent for domestic and international traffic but had denied the discounts to its rival Albacom.
Albacom, owned by Banca Nazionale del Lavoro British Telecom and Mediaset, offers telecom services for closed user groups.
The authority said that Telecom Italia had offered the discounts to closed user groups on its own network.

"Telecom refused to extend the application of the same tarrifs to Albacom, which had requested them for its own clients configured in closed user groups and which lodged a complaint with the antitrust authority," the statement said.

Telecoms closed user group services and those of its competitors "appear to present the same characteristics in every way and therefore fall within the services liberalised by community (EU) directives," the statement added.
The authority said Telecom's discounts "had the effect of inducing the client to prefer the service... supplied by the public operator rather than that offered by competitors."

"Such behaviour can seriously impede access by other suppliers to the liberalised market of advanced telephone services and could therefore be seen as an abuse of a dominant position," the statement added. Rome newsroom +392-6782505
